Find PWM motif hits in DNA sequences

Source: R/pwm-hits.R
gseq.pwm_hits.Rd

Returns every window of each sequence whose PWM score reaches score.thresh: the windows gseq.pwm(mode = "count") counts, with their positions, strand and score.

Usage

gseq.pwm_hits(
  seqs,
  pssm,
  score.thresh,
  bidirect = TRUE,
  strand = 1L,
  start_pos = NULL,
  end_pos = NULL,
  extend = FALSE,
  prior = 0.01
)

Arguments

seqs

character vector of DNA sequences (A/C/G/T/N; case-insensitive)

pssm

numeric matrix or data frame with columns named A, C, G, T (additional columns are allowed and will be ignored). Each row holds the probabilities or counts of the four bases at one motif position; log-odds matrices, NA values and rows summing to 0 are rejected.

score.thresh

single number; windows scoring at or above it are hits.

bidirect

logical; if TRUE, scans both strands (default: TRUE)

strand

integer; 1 for the forward strand, -1 for the reverse (default: 1). Used only when bidirect = FALSE, and required there - 0 is refused, since exactly one strand is read and 0 cannot name it. Under bidirect = TRUE both strands are read and this is ignored.

start_pos

integer or NULL; 1-based inclusive start of ROI (default: 1)

end_pos

integer or NULL; 1-based inclusive end of ROI (default: sequence length)

extend

logical or integer; how far past end_pos a window may run, as in gseq.pwm.

prior

numeric; pseudocount added to frequencies (default: 0.01). Set to 0 for no pseudocounts.

Value

A data frame with one row per hit and columns seq_idx (1-based index into seqs), start and end (1-based, inclusive window positions on the sequence), strand (1 or -1) and score, ordered by seq_idx and start. It has no rows when nothing passes.

Details

Windows are scored exactly as gseq.pwm scores them in "count" mode with its default neutral_chars and no spatial weights: a natural-log likelihood (including the prior), with a window holding N or any other non-ACGT character left out. Gap characters are not skipped - they are non-ACGT characters like any other - so on a sequence without gaps the number of hits per sequence equals gseq.pwm(mode = "count")'s count. Windows that cannot reach the threshold are skipped without being scored, which makes a strict threshold fast; the hits are the same as scoring every window.

Strand: under bidirect = TRUE a window is one hit, whose score is the log-sum-exp of its forward and reverse-complement scores (the value thresholded, as in gseq.pwm and pwm.count), and whose strand is the strand that scores higher on its own (1 on a tie), as gseq.pwm(mode = "pos") names it. Under bidirect = FALSE only the strand named by strand is read and strand is that strand. start and end are the window's positions on the input sequence whatever the strand.

See also

gseq.pwm, gintervals.pwm_hits for hits over genomic intervals.

Examples

pssm <- matrix(
    c(
        0.7, 0.1, 0.1, 0.1,
        0.1, 0.7, 0.1, 0.1,
        0.1, 0.1, 0.7, 0.1,
        0.1, 0.1, 0.1, 0.7
    ),
    ncol = 4, byrow = TRUE, dimnames = list(NULL, c("A", "C", "G", "T"))
)
seqs <- c("TTACGTAAACGTTT", "GGGGGGGG")
gseq.pwm_hits(seqs, pssm, score.thresh = -3)
#>   seq_idx start end strand     score
#> 1       1     3   6      1 -0.833697
#> 2       1     9  12      1 -0.833697

# the same windows gseq.pwm(mode = "count") counts
gseq.pwm(seqs, pssm, mode = "count", score.thresh = -3)
#> [1] 2 0
